shortItems.brief: On her first day at work, a new employee asks her coworker Noa to show her once how to arrange a small shelf display, then arranges it herself.

storyPattern.goal: Learn how to arrange a small display by watching it demonstrated
storyPattern.interaction: The new worker asks for one demonstration and then repeats the task independently
storyPattern.outcome: The new worker arranges the display without further help

storyPattern.goal: Choose one task to complete within a limited time
storyPattern.interaction: State a time constraint and agree which task takes priority

storyPattern.goal: Prepare a complete copy of a document for an appointment
storyPattern.interaction: Notice the cropped page and make a clearer copy
storyPattern.outcome: Keep the complete copy with the original

shortItems.brief: A tenant wants to hang a coat without drilling, asks the landlord if she can use a removable hook, gets his agreement, and puts it on the inside of the closet door.

storyPattern.goal: Hang a coat without making a permanent change
storyPattern.interaction: Explain the preferred no-drill option and ask before using it
storyPattern.outcome: Get agreement and attach the removable hook

shortItems.brief: Michal receives a call offering a home service visit at three o’clock, when she is at work. She asks for a later time, and they agree on a time when she can be home.

storyPattern.goal: Leave a bulky recyclable item in the right place

storyPattern.interaction: Explain the space constraint and choose a smaller item together

shortItems.brief: A woman sees a parcel notice on her way to work and asks her sister, who is at home, to collect the parcel later that afternoon. Her sister agrees.

storyPattern.interaction: Explain the scheduling need and propose a reciprocal swap

storyPattern.interaction: The mother explains the timing problem; the coordinator checks that the sister is listed; the mother confirms the pickup time with her sister
storyPattern.outcome: The sister agrees to collect the child, the coordinator is informed, and the child is collected as planned

stories.brief: Michal visits a public-service office to update her address after moving. storyPattern.outcome: Replace the incomplete copy, organize the file, and leave with a specific item to clarify

storyPattern.outcome: Print and check a corrected label before the sender hands over the parcel

stories.brief: A 1967 film about Jaffa’s Old City depicts its past and contemporary life, including art, fishing, markets and leisure; it ends with 19-year-old Avi Toledano singing a song that became closely associated with Jaffa.

sources.title: Jaffa - Sights and Sounds in the Old City | 1967
It is Jaffa, my Dear, it is Jaffa
Fishermen in Jaffa | 1962
Development of Jaffas Old City for Tourism and Arts
Preserving Urban Heritage: From Old Jaffa to Modern Tel Aviv
זוהי יפו – Words and performance
Becoming Mediterranean: Greek Popular Music and Ethno-Class Politics in Israel, 1952-1982

storyBeats: In 1967, Israel Film Service released a 13-minute documentary about Jaffa’s Old City, presenting both its ancient past and its life in the 1960s.
The film was directed by Baruch Dienar, photographed by Yehiel Neeman, and featured original music by Moshe Wilensky.
The documentary was made with the Hasbarah Center, Israel’s Tourism Ministry, the Association for Development of Old Jaffa, and the Tel Aviv-Yafo Municipality.
The film presented Old Jaffa at an early stage of its promotion as both a tourist destination and an artists’ colony.

A public company established by the Israeli government and Tel Aviv-Yafo Municipality in 1960 was tasked with developing Old Jaffa as a cultural and entertainment center while protecting religious and archaeological sites.
A separate 1967 newsreel describes reconstruction in an area called HaShetach HaGadol, with space being made for tourism, art, and entertainment.

A 1962 documentary about Jaffa’s fishermen describes them returning with their catch at dawn, bargaining with wholesalers over its price, eating at Benno’s tavern, resting, and going out to fish again at night.
The 1967 film ends with Avi Toledano singing “It Is Jaffa, My Dear, It Is Jaffa” at the Omar Khayyam club, over day and night views of the Old City.
The National Library’s music record identifies Yossi Gamzu as lyricist and Moshe Wilensky as composer of “Zohi Yafo.”

The film archive reports that Toledano was 19 during the performance and that the song became closely associated with Jaffa; the National Library record notes that singing it brought him early public recognition.

stories.brief: An Israeli newsreel depicts preparations for Passover, including a street-side cauldron used to boil and clean cooking utensils, and people shopping for dishes and matzah.

sources.title: Israelis Prepare for Passover as Incoming Tourism Augments
Passover: The Laws and Customs of Passover
Mikveh Israel Guide to Pesah
Baking Matzah for Export
Distribution of Passover Food Parcels to Poor Children

storyBeats: A two-minute Geva newsreel from 1953 records preparations for Passover in Israel and includes scenes at Haifa’s port.
On a city street, people set a large cauldron of water over a fire and immerse cooking dishes in it before the holiday.
The boiling-water process is called hagalah; it is used for suitable utensils that had been used with leavened food, so they can be prepared for Passover use.
The guide explains that utensils are cleaned before immersion and that the item must be fully submerged in boiling water; a large vessel can be used for this purpose.
The newsreel also records shoppers buying new dishes and matzah in stores as the holiday approaches.
Matzah is unleavened bread eaten during Passover; the holiday rules also require leavened foods to be excluded and certain cooking utensils to be prepared for holiday use.
The same newsreel shows women doing laundry in outdoor tubs, another household task taking place before the holiday.
The film records ships carrying tourists docking at Haifa ahead of Passover, with passengers loading luggage onto cars and visiting tourist sites.
A 1951 Israeli newsreel separately documents matzah being baked for export, showing that matzah production was also part of the country’s commercial activity.
A 1954 Israeli newsreel records food parcels being distributed to poor children for Passover, adding charitable assistance to the holiday preparations documented in the period’s newsreels.

stories.brief: A silent 1948 documentary records changing urban life in Israel, including new apartments near Tel Aviv, children playing, a market, work at Haifa port and scenes from Nazareth and Jerusalem.

sources.title: Urban Landscape in Israel | 1948
Urban Landscape in Tel Aviv-Yafo, 1950s–1970s: Yad Lebanim Boulevard

storyBeats: The silent documentary, produced by David Zeitani, is ten minutes long and records urban scenes in Israel in 1948.
Near Tel Aviv, the film records apartment buildings under construction among the dunes, in the neighborhoods of Kiryat Shalom and Kiryat Borochov.
Children are shown playing outdoors.
The documentary includes holidaymakers at the Ramat Aviv Hotel and on Tel Aviv’s beach.
A Tel Aviv market appears among the city scenes.
Scouts are shown walking in the street and planting trees on Tu Bishvat.
At Haifa port, workers unload a ship.
In Nazareth, the film records a monk at the Church of the Annunciation and a Christian funeral ceremony.
The Jerusalem scenes include Mea Shearim, the Old City, and central Jerusalem.
The film also records a ceremony laying the cornerstone of a new church.

The mother calls her sister with the pickup time, gets her agreement, and informs the coordinator. The sister collects the child as planned.

storyPattern.goal: Arrange a dependable change to a child's pickup plan when work runs late
storyPattern.relationship: A mother, her daughter, the after-school coordinator, and the mother's sister
storyPattern.interaction: The mother explains the delay and asks about her sister collecting the child; the coordinator verifies the sister is listed, and the mother confirms the time with her sister
storyPattern.outcome: The sister agrees to collect the child, the coordinator is informed, and the pickup happens as planned

stories.brief: Michal visits a public-service office after moving apartments to update her address record. Uri reviews her identification and rental agreement, points out the page showing the new address, and helps her replace a photocopy that cuts off the apartment number. Uri adds the complete copy to her file and gives her a note to clarify whether a recent electricity bill is needed.

storyPattern.goal: Prepare a document file for an address-related visit and identify any remaining question
storyPattern.relationship: Resident seeking help and public-service clerk reviewing her file
storyPattern.interaction: Review the documents brought, clarify which part shows the new address, and notice that a copy is incomplete
storyPattern.outcome: Replace the incomplete copy, organize the file, and leave with a specific item to clarify

stories.brief: Dana mails a small parcel from a post office in Be’er Sheva. She asks clerk Yossi where the return address belongs on the label, notices the apartment number is missing from the destination address, supplies it, and checks Yossi’s read-back and the legibility of both addresses. Yossi prints a corrected label, and Dana attaches it and hands over the parcel.

storyPattern.goal: Make sure a parcel label contains clear destination and return details
storyPattern.relationship: Parcel sender Dana and postal clerk Yossi
storyPattern.interaction: Dana asks where the return address belongs, supplies the missing apartment number, and checks Yossi’s read-back
storyPattern.outcome: Yossi prints a corrected label; Dana checks both addresses, attaches the label, and hands over the parcel

stories.brief: Ashkelon Municipality announced programs for children and families focused on healthy eating, physical activity and emotional well-being. One program involves 50 kindergartens; another engages about 500 students from 20 schools in health activities.

stories.brief: Israel Railways plans service changes from November 26–28 that affect routes used by Ashkelon passengers. The Ashkelon–Binyamina service will split into sections on November 26–27, with connecting buses and free shuttles described in the notice; passengers are advised to check trip details before departure.

stories.brief: A 1967 film about Jaffa’s Old City depicts its past and contemporary life, including art, fishing, markets and leisure; it ends with 19-year-old Avi Toledano singing a song that became closely associated with Jaffa.

sources.title: Jaffa - Sights and Sounds in the Old City | 1967
It is Jaffa, my Dear, it is Jaffa
Fishermen in Jaffa | 1962
Development of Jaffas Old City for Tourism and Arts
Preserving Urban Heritage: From Old Jaffa to Modern Tel Aviv
זוהי יפו – Words and performance
Becoming Mediterranean: Greek Popular Music and Ethno-Class Politics in Israel, 1952-1982

storyBeats: In 1967, Israel Film Service released a 13-minute documentary about Jaffa’s Old City, presenting both its ancient past and its life in the 1960s.
The film was directed by Baruch Dienar, photographed by Yehiel Neeman, and featured original music by Moshe Wilensky.
The documentary was made with the Hasbarah Center, Israel’s Tourism Ministry, the Association for Development of Old Jaffa, and the Tel Aviv-Yafo Municipality.
The film presented Old Jaffa at an early stage of its promotion as both a tourist destination and an artists’ colony.

A public company established by the Israeli government and Tel Aviv-Yafo Municipality in 1960 was tasked with developing Old Jaffa as a cultural and entertainment center while protecting religious and archaeological sites.
A separate 1967 newsreel describes reconstruction in an area called HaShetach HaGadol, with space being made for tourism, art, and entertainment.

A 1962 documentary about Jaffa’s fishermen describes them returning with their catch at dawn, bargaining with wholesalers over its price, eating at Benno’s tavern, resting, and going out to fish again at night.
The 1967 film ends with Avi Toledano singing “It Is Jaffa, My Dear, It Is Jaffa” at the Omar Khayyam club, over day and night views of the Old City.
The National Library’s music record identifies Yossi Gamzu as lyricist and Moshe Wilensky as composer of “Zohi Yafo.”

The film archive reports that Toledano was 19 during the performance and that the song became closely associated with Jaffa; the National Library record notes that singing it brought him early public recognition.

stories.brief: An Israeli newsreel depicts preparations for Passover, including a street-side cauldron used to boil and clean cooking utensils, and people shopping for dishes and matzah.

sources.title: Israelis Prepare for Passover as Incoming Tourism Augments
Passover: The Laws and Customs of Passover
Mikveh Israel Guide to Pesah
Baking Matzah for Export
Distribution of Passover Food Parcels to Poor Children

storyBeats: A two-minute Geva newsreel from 1953 records preparations for Passover in Israel and includes scenes at Haifa’s port.
On a city street, people set a large cauldron of water over a fire and immerse cooking dishes in it before the holiday.
The boiling-water process is called hagalah; it is used for suitable utensils that had been used with leavened food, so they can be prepared for Passover use.
The guide explains that utensils are cleaned before immersion and that the item must be fully submerged in boiling water; a large vessel can be used for this purpose.
The newsreel also records shoppers buying new dishes and matzah in stores as the holiday approaches.
Matzah is unleavened bread eaten during Passover; the holiday rules also require leavened foods to be excluded and certain cooking utensils to be prepared for holiday use.
The same newsreel shows women doing laundry in outdoor tubs, another household task taking place before the holiday.
The film records ships carrying tourists docking at Haifa ahead of Passover, with passengers loading luggage onto cars and visiting tourist sites.
A 1951 Israeli newsreel separately documents matzah being baked for export, showing that matzah production was also part of the country’s commercial activity.
A 1954 Israeli newsreel records food parcels being distributed to poor children for Passover, adding charitable assistance to the holiday preparations documented in the period’s newsreels.

stories.brief: A silent 1948 documentary records changing urban life in Israel, including new apartments near Tel Aviv, children playing, a market, work at Haifa port and scenes from Nazareth and Jerusalem.

sources.title: Urban Landscape in Israel | 1948
Urban Landscape in Tel Aviv-Yafo, 1950s–1970s: Yad Lebanim Boulevard

storyBeats: The silent documentary, produced by David Zeitani, is ten minutes long and records urban scenes in Israel in 1948.
Near Tel Aviv, the film records apartment buildings under construction among the dunes, in the neighborhoods of Kiryat Shalom and Kiryat Borochov.
Children are shown playing outdoors.
The documentary includes holidaymakers at the Ramat Aviv Hotel and on Tel Aviv’s beach.
A Tel Aviv market appears among the city scenes.
Scouts are shown walking in the street and planting trees on Tu Bishvat.
At Haifa port, workers unload a ship.
In Nazareth, the film records a monk at the Church of the Annunciation and a Christian funeral ceremony.
The Jerusalem scenes include Mea Shearim, the Old City, and central Jerusalem.
The film also records a ceremony laying the cornerstone of a new church.
